ai.title: Fix str replace on Windows newlines
ai.summary: Refactor processStrReplace to normalize line endings before matching and replacing. Moved normalizeLineEndings to module scope and applied to newStr. Deferred line ending restoration until after all replacements. Covers backend/src/process-str-replace.ts.

eli5.text: Text replacement in the backend now works correctly on Windows-style line breaks, so edits that span multiple lines won't silently fail or miss matches when the file uses carriage-return-plus-newline formatting. The system now normalizes all line endings internally before matching and replacing, then restores the original style at the end of the whole operation. This affects the internal assistant editor's text replacement feature. It is live today.

You might notice the agent list updates on its own roughly once a minute rather than requiring a manual refresh, and this is live today.

ai.title: Add simple-code-reviewer agent
ai.summary: New `.agents/simple-code-reviewer.ts` defines a `simple-code-reviewer` agent using `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4` to review local code changes via `git diff`, untracked files, and spawned `codebuff/file-explorer@0.0.2` agents. `.agents/git-committer.ts` removes `process_type: 'SYNC'` and `timeout_seconds: 30` from `git diff` and `git log` tool calls, relying on default terminal command behavior. Scope limited to `.agents/` directory; no user-facing CLI or Web changes.

eli5.text: The system now has a new helper that can automatically review code changes before they are finalized. When someone on the development team asks for a review, this helper looks at what changed using the project's version history tool, reads the affected files, and brings in another helper to find any related files that might be affected. It then gives written feedback on what could be improved. This only affects the internal team's workflow and does not change anything you see as a user today.

ai.title: Switch package manager from yarn to bun
ai.summary: Updated the `packageManager` field in `package.json` from `yarn@1.22.22` to `bun@1.0.0`. This change aligns the project's package management with Bun, potentially improving installation speeds and compatibility with modern JavaScript tooling. The modification affects the root configuration file, ensuring that all contributors use the specified package manager.

eli5.text: The project has switched the tool used to install and manage the code libraries the app depends on, moving from one provider to a newer one in the project's main configuration file. This only affects people who build or modify the app's source code on their own computers, such as developers and contributors. If you looked at the configuration file, you would see that single line about the install tool has been changed from the old name to the new one. No changes to the app's features are expected.

ai.title: SDK build creates colocated index.d.ts files
ai.summary: sdk/build.ts now writes dist/esm/index.d.ts and dist/cjs/index.d.ts after bundling, re-exporting from sdk/src/index. package.json types and exports.types fields point to ./dist/esm/index.d.ts instead of the nested sdk/src path. This ensures TypeScript resolves declarations colocated with the bundle index.js for both ESM and CJS consumers.

eli5.text: When developers install the SDK tool into their projects, their code editors will now correctly find the built-in instructions that explain what functions and types are available. Previously, TypeScript tools could point to a temporary file path that didn't always exist after installation, causing confusing code hints; now those instructions sit right next to the installed files so they're reliable. This affects only developers using the SDK in TypeScript-based projects.
